newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, CRICKET - Atherton happy with tough leadup matches.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, CRICKET - Atherton happy with tough leadup matches.

text.p: PALMERSTON North, Jan 13 - England cricket captain Mike Atherton wants high calibre opposition for his team in their leadup to the first test against New Zealand in Auckland next week, NZPA reports.
So he was delighted to find England up against eight current or former test players in the New Zealand Selection, who begin their four-day match against the tourists at Fitzherbert Park today.
The English squad had two leadup matches to the first of the three tests against New Zealand and they're keen to get as much worth out of them as possible.
The second match, also a four-day fixture, is against Northern Districts at Hamilton starting on Saturday.
Given the option of softer opposition in the buildup to the test series, Atherton has no doubts which way he'd rather go.
"I'd much prefer to play against them (the top players) early in our tour," he told NZPA.
"We can have a good look at them, and playing a very strong standard of opposition you've got to lift your game as well, so I'm all for that."
Atherton appreciates the value of a victory against strong opponents.
"You've got to get into winning habits and that's what we've got to try and do in the next two games.
"Good form is not a thing you can turn on and off like a tap.
"I want good performances in both games. If you get them, the results take care of themselves.
"I want individuals playing well, with high confidence, before the big matches.
"It's an important couple of weeks for us."
Opening batsman Atherton also knows it is a crucial time for him.
He was out of the runs on the Zimbabwean leg of England's tour, collecting just 34 in four test innings and 66 in three one-day internationals.
But he is content with his touch, and has the backing of coach David Lloyd.
"I'm feeling pretty good," he said.
"I've had lots of nets in New Zealand and I feel as though I'm hitting the ball pretty well.
"But it would be nice to get in the middle and score a few runs."
Lloyd was effusive over what he saw from Atherton in the nets here yesterday.
"I thought he batted quite beautifully," said Lloyd, himself a former test opener.
"He's in good heart and he feels better with his own form."
